title: zhouxiaoka/autoclip
lede: AutoClip is an MIT-licensed desktop app that takes a link to a long interview, podcast or course and cuts it into short clips with subtitles, cover images and post copy.

points: Targets Douyin, Xiaohongshu, TikTok, Reels, YouTube Shorts, Bilibili and YouTube, following each platform's aspect ratio and length rules.
Scores candidate moments and renders up to 10 clips per platform, keeping the rest as alternates you can generate later.
Cutting, speaker framing and rendering happen locally; analysis uses a cloud API with your own key or a local model through Ollama or LM Studio.
Subtitles come from the source video, local Whisper or SenseVoice, or a configured cloud transcription service.
Available as a desktop app for Apple Silicon Macs and Windows x64, plus Docker, a CLI and an MCP server sharing one pipeline.

points.text: Provider setup is the most common pain point: API keys that will not save, models that cannot be switched, and failing connection checks.
Connections to specific providers break, including OpenAI from a Windows Docker install and Alibaba Cloud Bailian.
Users want clearer failure reporting; one says runs errored mid-way with credits spent and no explanation.
Exported subtitles use a thin, boxed font rather than the bold captions shown in the editor preview.
The Windows desktop build can stall during generation.
